about: Hermann J. Wiemer grew up in Bernkastel on Germany’s Mosel, where his father ran a vine-grafting research station and taught him to graft Riesling onto American rootstock. He came to New York in 1965, saw the Mosel in Seneca Lake’s steep slopes and cool climate, and in 1973 bought a farm on the lake’s west shore near Dundee. His winery opened in 1979 and became one of the pioneers of Finger Lakes Riesling. Since 2007 it has been run by his former apprentice Fred Merwarth and partner Oskar Bynke.

The Dry Riesling is the estate’s signature wine, a blend drawn from each of Wiemer’s vineyards on the western side of Seneca Lake. In 2021 the fruit came in over 17 separate hand pickings between late September and the end of October, each lot hand sorted, pressed as whole clusters and fermented with the grapes’ own wild yeasts. The small lots are then blended for texture and balance, and the wine is bottled without fining agents.

The winery describes the 2021 as opening with the scent of spring blossoms, followed by a succulent palate of early-season fruit kept in line by crisp acidity, with a fine texture, a long finish and the mineral edge that runs through the house style. It is technically dry, with just under seven grams of residual sugar balancing the lake’s bright acidity, which makes it an unusually versatile partner at the table.
facts: Whole-cluster pressed, wild-yeast fermented in small lots, no fining agents
